tools.name: meetings-venv
tools.licenceNote: The meetings pillar's own virtual environment of the python tool, with the pip it bundles (MIT), so its numpy pin never meets another pillar's packages in the shared venv.

run: import sys, pip; print('meetings-venv', sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix, 'pip', pip.__version__)

tools.name: sherpa-onnx
tools.licenceNote: sherpa-onnx and sherpa-onnx-core (Apache-2.0, with the onnxruntime it carries inside, MIT) and numpy (BSD-3-Clause, with 0BSD, MIT, Zlib and CC0-1.0 parts), wheels only, into the meetings venv. Runs only in a separate Python process with the network blocked.

run: import sherpa_onnx, numpy; print('sherpa-onnx', sherpa_onnx.__version__, 'numpy', numpy.__version__)

tools.name: parakeet-tdt-v2
tools.licenceNote: NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 weights (CC-BY-4.0: credit NVIDIA), as sherpa-onnx's int8 ONNX export, kept as downloaded. Loaded only by sherpa-onnx in the transcriber's own process.

run: import sys, numpy as np, sherpa_onnx as so; d = sys.argv[1]; r = so.OfflineRecognizer.from_transducer(encoder=d + '/encoder.int8.onnx', decoder=d + '/decoder.int8.onnx', joiner=d + '/joiner.int8.onnx', tokens=d + '/tokens.txt', num_threads=2, model_type='nemo_transducer', decoding_method='greedy_search'); s = r.create_stream(); s.accept_waveform(16000, np.zeros(16000, dtype=np.float32)); r.decode_stream(s); print('parakeet-tdt-v2 decoded', len(s.result.tokens), 'tokens of silence')

tools.name: pyannote-segmentation
tools.licenceNote: pyannote segmentation-3.0 (MIT, CNRS), as sherpa-onnx's ONNX export with its licence file, kept as downloaded; needs no Hugging Face token. Loaded only by sherpa-onnx in the transcriber's own process.

run: import sys, sherpa_onnx as so; c = so.OfflineSpeakerSegmentationModelConfig(pyannote=so.OfflineSpeakerSegmentationPyannoteModelConfig(model=sys.argv[1]), num_threads=1); print('pyannote-segmentation', 'valid' if c.validate() else 'invalid')

tools.name: wespeaker-resnet34-lm
tools.licenceNote: WeSpeaker's ResNet34-LM speaker embedding trained on VoxCeleb; WeSpeaker's pretrained models carry their training data's licence, VoxCeleb's CC-BY-4.0 (credit WeSpeaker and VoxCeleb). sherpa-onnx's ONNX export, kept as downloaded. Loaded only by sherpa-onnx in the transcriber's own process.

run: import sys, numpy as np, sherpa_onnx as so; x = so.SpeakerEmbeddingExtractor(so.SpeakerEmbeddingExtractorConfig(model=sys.argv[1], num_threads=1)); s = x.create_stream(); s.accept_waveform(16000, (np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(32000) * 0.1).astype(np.float32)); s.input_finished(); print('wespeaker-resnet34-lm dim', len(x.compute(s)))

tools.name: silero-vad
tools.licenceNote: Silero VAD v4 (MIT, Silero Team), as k2-fsa exported it to ONNX with only the 16 kHz branch, kept as downloaded. Loaded only by sherpa-onnx in the transcriber's own process.

run: import sys, numpy as np, sherpa_onnx as so; c = so.VadModelConfig(); c.silero_vad.model = sys.argv[1]; c.sample_rate = 16000; v = so.VoiceActivityDetector(c, buffer_size_in_seconds=10); v.accept_waveform(np.zeros(16000, dtype=np.float32)); v.flush(); print('silero-vad ran, speech found:', not v.empty())
